Red Bull Marketing Strategy: How Red Bull Became a Global Lifestyle Brand

D

Written by

DigionTop Team

Red Bull is more than an energy drink. It is now a global lifestyle brand and is a symbol of adventure, extreme sports, entertainment, speed and high performance. It is one of the most successful examples of how to develop a company's image and identity rather than just a product.

The Red Bull Marketing Strategy is all about experiences, engaging content, event sponsorships, athlete relationships, and digital media. Red Bull is not telling people to drink its product over and over, it's making content and experiences that people want to watch and share.

What Makes Red Bull Marketing Strategy Different?

Product features, price, discount and traditional advertising are all key concerns of many beverage companies. Rather, Red Bull went another way.

The company surrounded itself with a strong concept: "energy, excitement, adventure and performance".

This positioning is complemented by its famous message “Gives You Wings.” Throughout, the brand has always been able to align its product with people who desire to do more, feel more exciting and take more chances.

This cohesive branding has resulted in Red Bull being recognizable to the people of different countries and different audiences.

1. Strong Brand Positioning

The Red Bull brand positioning is one of the biggest strengths in the Red Bull brand strategy.

Red Bull isn't just another energy drink. It offers itself as a vibrant and adventurous way of life.

It is marketed as to evoke the brand's association with:

  • Extreme sports

  • Adventure

  • Fitness and performance

  • Music and entertainment

  • Racing

  • Gaming

  • Travel

Children and young people that are young and energetic.

This positioning is advantageous for Red Bull in a competitive beverage market.

The take-home message is straightforward: A good brand is supposed to stand for an idea, not a product.

2. Content Marketing Is at the Heart of Red Bull

Red Bull has established a reputation for itself in the field of content marketing. The company doesn't just use ads to create their media and entertainment, they make it on their own.

Red Bull creates videos, articles, documentaries, social media, interviews, event coverage and more.

This way, the brand resembles a media company rather than a traditional beverage company.

For instance, Red Bull could feature an athlete completing an amazing feat, instead of actively pushing an energy drink. The audience sees the story because it is interesting; the Red Bull brand becomes naturally associated with the story itself.

It's an effective illustration of brand storytelling.

3. Red Bull and Extreme Sports

Red Bull's global marketing strategy is heavily dependent upon sports marketing.

The brand has established good links with extreme sports like:

  • Formula 1

  • Skydiving

  • Mountain biking

  • Surfing

  • Snowboarding

  • Skateboarding

  • Motocross

  • Cliff diving

These activities reflect the personality that Red Bull wants to convey.

Rather than just putting their logo on a sporting event, Red Bull often becomes so much a part of the experience, the athlete or the event itself.

This will make the marketing more realistic and memorable.

4. The Power of Experiential Marketing

Another important aspect to the Red Bull marketing strategy is experiential marketing.

The company designs experiences that people can do, watch, take photos of, and share.

The Red Bull Stratos project is one of the most popular, with Felix Baumgartner jumping from the stratosphere in 2012.

A tremendous amount of attention was focused on the event and it sparked a lot of online conversation.

What is key here is that memorable experiences can create marketing value that is more than a typical ad.

5. Red Bull Uses Social Media Effectively

Red Bull has made itself at home on social media.

The brand doesn't post product-oriented content on their social media, but rather posts exciting and visually appealing content.

It is typically comprised of the following content:

  • Sports highlights

  • Athlete stories

  • Behind-the-scenes videos

  • Adventure content

  • Event clips

  • Short-form videos

  • Inspirational stories

  • Entertainment

This is a good idea for Red Bull to engage with people who like their content.

This is a key distinction between content marketing and traditional advertising. However, good content can draw attention even when the product itself is not the main focus.

6. Athlete and Influencer Partnerships

Red Bull collaborates with sportsmen and personalities that are the perfect fit for the brand.

Such collaborations enable the company to access specific markets and enhance trust.

For instance, a sportsman linked with Red Bull can bring the brand to the people who are fascinated with a particular sport or activity.

What is crucial is that the relationship must be authentic. Red Bull selects personalities whose lifestyle is already in line with Red Bull.

This is a great lesson for companies implementing an influencer marketing program—relevancy is more important than size of audience.

7. Red Bull Builds Communities

Community building is also an important aspect of Red Bull's branding.

The company brings people together based on common interests in sports, music, gaming, adventure and entertainment.

People feel more connected with a brand when they relate to these communities.

This makes customers more than buyers. They can be the brand's followers of its content and lifestyle.

Community-based marketing can be particularly effective as it is a natural phenomenon that people share all kinds of content and experiences that are of their interest.

8. Red Bull's Digital Marketing Approach

It is based on a mix of video, social media, websites, online publications, events and community engagement.

The brand is aware that the modern audience does not want to see ads at every turn. They are looking for entertainment, information, inspiration and experiences.

That's why Red Bull produces content that will get people to notice it instead of just buying it.

The same is true for businesses to promote their online store, professional service, startup or digital marketing service.

It's all about building content that adds value and makes people want to follow the brand.

9. Consistent Brand Identity

Red Bull's success is also due to consistency.

The brand has a consistent ‘personality’ in each of the marketing channels.

It is normally associated with communication:

  • Energy

  • Adventure

  • Creativity

  • Performance

  • Excitement

  • Courage

This uniformity helps the brand get recognized.

This can be done on a low budget, and does not require a large marketing budget for a business. A consistent brand message, tone, visual style and values can create a strong identity even for a small company.

10. What Businesses Can Learn From Red Bull

There are some lessons that can be learnt from the Red Bull marketing strategy, and these lessons can be helpful for marketers and business owners.

Not a product, an Experience!

Advertisements tend to be forgotten, customers tend to remember the experience. Building an unforgettable experience can add value to a brand.

Generate Content People Desire to Consume.

Don't just go about pushing products: develop content to educate, entertain, inspire, or solve problems.

Create a clear brand identity.

Customers can easily identify a company by its recognition of identity.

Use Storytelling

Stories can elicit emotion and help to make marketing messages stick in people's minds.

Use the right communities to connect with.

Identify the communities that are most appropriate for your brand and produce content geared toward their interests.

Be Consistent

Effective branding is a process. Reducing variability through website, social media, advertising and other channels can help to reinforce recognition.

Overall Summary

It's not just about selling an energy drink that makes Red Bull a success. The power of its growth lies in its ability to construct an energy, adventure, entertainment and performance lifestyle brand.

The Red Bull Marketing Strategy is an example of how these can be effectively combined to build an unforgettable brand and influence the world.

One of the most important points to take is that successful marketing campaigns are not necessarily about getting people to hear more about the product. At times, the best approach is to make something that people really want to see, do, talk about and share.

This has been the way Red Bull was able to build a brand that is a known entity worldwide and make an energy drink a lifestyle brand.
